In these, various strate- gies may be adopted to reduce risk where possible, includ- ing the use of regional anaesthesia or total intravenous anaesthesia with propofol (but see also p.1793), avoidance of nitrous oxide, minimal use of opioids, adequate hydra- tion (especially with colloids), and possibly the use of in- traoperative supplemental oxygen (although not all studies found this of benefit).13,14 Avoidance of high-dose neostig- mine (limiting the dose to a maximum of 2.5 mg in adults) has also been suggested.14 There is evidence that some nonpharmacological interventions, such as acupuncture of the P6 point, may also be effective, especially for nausea.21 Many types of drugs have been tried as prophylactic antiemetics. These include the 5-HT3 antagonists, pheno- thiazines such as prochlorperazine, butyrophenones such as droperidol, antihistamines such as promethazine, cy- clizine, or dimenhydrinate, and some other drugs such as dexamethasone and hyoscine.16,20 A large and well- designed multicentre study (the IMPACT trial) has shown that ondansetron, droperidol, and dexamethasone are of similar efficacy;22 it also confirmed that avoidance of vol- atile anaesthetics and nitrous oxide was of as much benefit in preventing PONV as use of a prophylactic antiemetic. The evidence suggests that other 5-HT3 antagonists are of similar efficacy to ondansetron.14 Evidence for some of the older drugs is less extensive, although benefit has often been shown in individual studies.13,14 Systematic reviews have confirmed the benefit of prophylaxis with dimen- hydrinate23 and transdermal hyoscine24 but have suggested that metoclopramide, which has been widely used, is in fact of little value in preventing PONV,25,26 perhaps be- cause the doses used are too low.26 However, another sys- tematic review27 included metoclopramide in a list of drugs that reliably prevented PONV compared with place- bo; other drugs listed were cyclizine, dexamethasone, do- lasetron, droperidol, granisetron, ondansetron, and tropi- setron. Ginger root has also been suggested, but again does not seem to be effective in this context,28 although there is some evidence of benefit for intramuscular ephedrine.29 Clonidine has also been reported to produce benefit,30,31 1702 Gastrointestinal Drugs possibly secondary to reduced sympathetic tone and lower use of inhalation anaesthetics and opioids.
